_readme: STARTER PACK — authored to be REPLACED by upstream. JSON has no comment syntax, so this
key is the header comment; the loader ignores unknown keys.
Nobody at Sparkle is an authority on what the law says. The HumaneBench project and
community are expected to define and maintain the real packs; this exists so the
mechanism has something to run against on day one.
Every 'guidance' string below is a NON-AUTHORITATIVE PLAIN-LANGUAGE PARAPHRASE. The
'source' URL governs. Effective dates are the pack author's reading of the instrument
and must be confirmed by counsel.
The Directive itself sets functional accessibility requirements; conformity is presumed
via the harmonised standard EN 301 549, which incorporates WCAG 2.1 level AA. The
checks below name the WCAG success criterion because that is the testable artefact, and
cite the Directive as the instrument because that is what has legal force.
A check binds to a detector by ID, and there is no deterministic detector for every
criterion. SC 4.1.3 is therefore authored as a JUDGED check rather than pointed at a
detector id that does not exist: a judged check that asks is honest, a detector check
that can never fire is a silent hole. The loader REJECTS a pack naming an unregistered
detector, so this cannot regress quietly.
This pack never asserts compliance. A check that does not fire means nothing fired —
not that a product is lawful.
instrument: Directive (EU) 2019/882 (European Accessibility Act), via EN 301 549 / WCAG 2.1 AA
notice: Guidance text is a non-authoritative paraphrase; the source URL governs. WCAG criteria are cited as the testable expression of the Directive's functional requirements, not as law in themselves.

checks.title: Every control must be operable from the keyboard
checks.guidance: that all functionality be operable through a keyboard interface, without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes

checks.article: Annex I (EN 301 549 / WCAG 2.1 SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content)
checks.title: Non-text content needs a text alternative
checks.guidance: that images, icons and other non-text content carry a text alternative serving the equivalent purpose, so it can be rendered as speech, braille or larger text

checks.article: Annex I (EN 301 549 / WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages)
checks.title: Status messages must reach assistive technology

detect.question: Does this change show a status update a sighted user would notice — a save confirmation, an inline validation error, a progress or result count — without exposing it to assistive technology, so a screen-reader user would never learn it happened?

checks.guidance: that a status change a sighted user would see — a saved confirmation, an error, a progress update — be exposed to assistive technology without moving focus

checks.article: Annex I (EN 301 549 / WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color)
checks.title: Colour must not be the only way meaning is conveyed
checks.guidance: that colour never be the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response or distinguishing an element
